alignments.note: Verbless Greek clause whose predicate is the interrogative adverb; under rules 53 and 62 the adverbial predicate carries the ASV's supplied verb, so the italicized *come* rides with `Πόθεν` rather than with the subject noun. Rule 63 points the same way, the subject being a lexical noun. Rule 17 heads the unit on *Whence*, the word that glosses the lexeme, not on the supplied verb.
Subject noun stands bare, the supplied verb having gone to the predicate adverb under rules 53 and 63.
Second interrogative adverb analysed exactly as s001, which is rule 24's habit; the repeated supplied *come* is its helper under rules 53 and 62.
Expressed preposition realized by *among* under rule 36.
Governed pronoun on its own English word under rule 2.
Ordinary negative aligned to *not*. No negative indefinite stands in the clause, so rules 41 and 59 do not arise, and the question is not interrogative `μή` under rule 44.

The clause expresses no subject and no verb; the adverb is its predicate, so under rules 53, 62 and 68 it carries both the supplied subject pronoun *they* and the supplied verb *come*, discontinuously under rule 15. Head on *hence*, the word glossing `ἐντεῦθεν`.

Supplied appositional *even* introducing the prepositional appositive *of your pleasures*, which `ἐκ` carries: it is a rule 7 helper on that preposition and rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics from making it `added`, headed on *of* under rule 17. The corpus folds a supplied *even* onto an expressed preposition in every one of its ten such units and marks none `added` — GAL.1.15 `ἐκ` → *even from*, the identical lemma and unhedged, with 2CO.10.16 `εἰς` → *even unto*, 2CO.1.19 `διά` → *even by*, GAL.5.14 and 1JN.5.20 `ἐν` → *even in*, and the improper prepositions at PHP.2.8, REV.12.11, REV.14.20, REV.18.5 and 2CO.12.2. Marking it `added` under rule 5 remains defensible and was the earlier reading here; it is declined because rule 98 is scoped in terms to an asyndetic seam between two like constituents both rendered alike — two infinitives, two participles, two adjectives — and *hence* and *of your pleasures* are an adverb and a prepositional phrase in apposition, with the second member introduced by an expressed token. Every `added` bare *even* in the corpus stands where no preposition introduces the appositive.
Rule 20: the genitive pronoun `ὑμῶν` is free — rule 76's availability test — and takes the supplied possessive *your*, so the article realizes nothing.
Noun on *pleasures*, its determiner slot occupied by the possessive that belongs to `ὑμῶν`.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive *your* under rule 20.

Second attributive article, following a head noun the Greek expresses (`ἡδονῶν`); rule 31's test makes the supplied relativizer the participle's helper and leaves this article its own `unrepresented` unit under rule 23. The determiner slot on the noun side is already taken by *your*, so nothing is left here either.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the relativizer *that* is its helper under rules 7 and 31, and rule 17 heads the unit on the lexical verb *war*.
Expressed preposition realized by *in* under rule 36.
Rule 20 again: `ὑμῶν` is free to take *your*, so the article realizes nothing; the dative case is left unmarked in English by the preposition's own *in*.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive *your* under rule 20, parallel to s013.

review_notes: One change from the accepted alignment: the italicized *even* (t014) is taken off `ἐκ` and marked `added`. `ἐκ` keeps only *of*. Rule 98 governs — an asyndetic seam between two like constituents both rendered alike, here *hence* and *of your pleasures* — and its governing precedent 2CO.3.7 concedes nothing; JAS.1.27 already reads a supplied juncture this way in this book. Rule 82 fixes a bare *even* as the gloss of `καί`, and no `καί` stands in the verse. The accepted reading (rule 7 helper on the preposition, rule 11 against the italics) is stated in the unit note and remains defensible; a later reader who prefers it need only merge t014 back into the s010 unit, head unchanged on *of*.

Everything else is unchanged. The three verbless clauses are the substance of the verse: both `πόθεν` clauses and the `ἐντεῦθεν` clause supply their verbs in English, and under rules 53, 62 and 68 those supplied words ride with the adverbial predicates, not with the subject nouns and not off the ASV's word order. `ἐντεῦθεν` additionally carries the supplied subject *they*, its clause expressing no subject at all (rule 68), discontinuously under rule 15.

All three articles are `unrepresented`. s011 and s017 are rule 20 displacement — a free `ὑμῶν` stands for each, and rule 76's availability test is satisfied since neither pronoun is spent on anything else. s014 is a second attributive article after an expressed head noun, so rule 31 gives the relativizer *that* to the participle and rule 23 empties the article. No supplied determiner stands anywhere in the verse for rules 51, 60 or 102 to hand an article.

`ἐν` is aligned twice, to *among* and to *in*, under rule 36; rule 21's determinerless clause is not in play, since an expressed preposition stands in each phrase and the articles carry no determiner.
